evals.prompt:
hey can you review my linkedin profile? i'm applying to staff pm roles at ai startups and want to make sure it's good. here it is:

Headline: Senior Product Manager at Acme Corp

About: I'm a passionate product manager with 8 years of experience building products that customers love. I have a track record of working cross-functionally to deliver results. I love solving hard problems and I'm always looking for new challenges.

Experience:
Acme Corp — Senior Product Manager (2021–present)
- Led development of new analytics dashboard
- Worked with engineering and design on feature roadmap
- Managed relationships with key stakeholders
- Helped improve retention metrics
- Supported go-to-market efforts for new product launches

Previous Corp — Product Manager (2018–2021)
- Owned the mobile app experience
- Collaborated with cross-functional teams
- Ran user research sessions
- Shipped several major features

Featured: (nothing)

Skills: Product Management, Roadmapping, Agile, JIRA, SQL, Stakeholder Management, User Research
evals.expected_output: Full panel review with section scores, three reviewer perspectives with specific quoted feedback, top 5 prioritized rewrites, and an offer to rewrite specific sections. Should call out weak/vague bullets, missing outcomes, generic about section, no featured section, and poor keyword coverage for AI roles.
assertions: Output includes a section-by-section scoring table covering Headline, About, Experience, Featured, and Skills
Output includes all three reviewer perspectives: Recruiter, Hiring Manager, and Head of Product
Each reviewer gives a numeric score (e.g. X/10)
Output quotes or directly references specific text from the profile (e.g. 'I'm a passionate product manager' or 'Helped improve retention metrics')
Output includes a prioritized list of top rewrites or edits
Output identifies the lack of outcomes or metrics in experience bullets
Output flags that the About section is generic or uses filler language
Output identifies the missing Featured section as a gap
Output offers to rewrite specific sections

evals.prompt:
I have a recruiter screen coming up next week for a Group PM role at a Series B AI company and I want to make sure my LinkedIn is dialed in before they look me up. Can you review it?

Headline: Group PM | AI Products & Platform | ex-Google, Stripe

About: I build AI products that solve real business problems. At Google, I led the launch of an ML-powered search ranking feature that improved click-through rates by 22% across 400M daily active users. At Stripe, I owned the fraud detection product roadmap, reducing false positives by 34% while maintaining <0.1% fraud rate. Now I'm looking for my next challenge — ideally a company where AI is core to the product, not a bolt-on.

Experience:
Stripe — Group Product Manager, Fraud & Risk (2020–2024)
- Defined and owned the 3-year roadmap for Stripe's fraud detection platform
- Led a team of 4 PMs, 2 data scientists, and 18 engineers across 3 time zones
- Reduced false positive rate by 34% through ML model improvements, saving merchants ~$120M in blocked revenue annually
- Launched real-time risk scoring API, now used by 60% of Stripe's enterprise customers
- Partnered with legal and compliance to ship GDPR-compliant risk signals across EU markets

Google — Senior Product Manager, Search (2016–2020)
- Led 0→1 development of ML-powered ranking feature (BERT integration) across Google Search
- Improved CTR by 22% on informational queries (400M DAU)
- Managed external partnerships with 3 content providers for training data acquisition
- Drove alignment across 6 engineering teams through weekly roadmap reviews

Featured: 1 article on AI product management on Medium (2022)

Skills: Product Strategy, AI/ML Products, Roadmapping, Cross-functional Leadership, Risk & Fraud, Platform Products, SQL, Python, OKRs
evals.expected_output: Review should acknowledge this is a strong profile with real outcomes. Should still find specific improvement opportunities. Should not be uniformly critical — most section scores should be 7+ out of 10. Should cite specific strengths by quoting the profile.
assertions: Output includes a section-by-section scoring table
Output includes all three reviewer perspectives: Recruiter, Hiring Manager, and Head of Product
Scores for Experience sections are 7 or higher out of 10 (reflecting the strong outcome-driven bullets)
Output acknowledges specific strengths with direct quotes or references from the profile
Output still identifies at least 2-3 specific improvement opportunities (not just generic praise)
Output includes a prioritized rewrite list
Output offers to rewrite specific sections

evals.prompt:
I'm a PM at a fintech company, been doing this for 6 years, and I'm passively open to Staff or Principal PM roles. My LinkedIn feels stale but I don't know exactly what's wrong. Can you take a look?

Headline: Product Manager | Fintech | Payments | Boston

About: Product manager with experience in financial services and payments technology. Skilled in working with engineering and design to ship products. Previous experience in consulting before transitioning to product.

Experience:
PaymentsCo — Product Manager (2019–present)
- Led redesign of onboarding flow, resulting in 18% improvement in activation rate
- Owned payments infrastructure roadmap for SMB segment ($40M ARR)
- Drove adoption of new pricing model across 3 customer segments, increasing ARPU by 12%
- Built and maintained relationships with key enterprise accounts
- Managed backlog and sprint ceremonies for team of 8 engineers

McKinsey & Company — Business Analyst (2015–2019)
- Worked on digital transformation projects for financial services clients
- Supported product strategy engagements
- Developed client presentations and recommendations

Featured: (empty)
Skills: Fintech, Payments, Product Management, SQL, Agile, Roadmapping, Stakeholder Management, Figma
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose: headline lacks level signal, About is thin and leads with consulting background, experience bullets are mixed quality (some good metrics, some weak), McKinsey role needs reframing. Should offer concrete rewrites.
assertions: Output includes a section-by-section scoring table
Output includes all three reviewer perspectives: Recruiter, Hiring Manager, and Head of Product
Output flags that the headline lacks level signal or seniority indicator for Staff/Principal roles
Output identifies the About section as underdeveloped or too thin
Output distinguishes between stronger bullets (with metrics) and weaker ones (task-oriented) in the PaymentsCo role
Output addresses how to reframe or improve the McKinsey/consulting background for PM audiences
Output includes a prioritized rewrite list
Output offers to rewrite specific sections
